articles.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
articles.excerpt:
Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

Massive scale, prime drilling locations, and advanced technologies help publicly traded oil and gas producers maintain their edge on production. articles.title: Global Market: Singapore core inflation hits nearly two-year high in August
articles.excerpt:
In August, Singapore's core inflation rose to 2.2%, surpassing both the prior month's rate and expectations. Headline consumer price inflation also climbed to 2.3% year-on-year, indicating ongoing price pressures. The central bank anticipates that inflation levels will remain high into the following year. Moreover, the economic growth outlook for 2026 was notably increased to between 4.5% and 5.5%, highlighting the lasting challenges of inflation management amidst robust economic growth.
